desc: ICOR's Mini-CALIBER is a compact, lightweight EOD robot for confined spaces, stairwells and under-vehicle inspection where a full-size platform cannot reach. It carries a manipulator and cameras for reconnaissance and small-charge render-safe tasks.

name: Rhyno Protect
desc: Shark Robotics' Rhyno Protect is a tracked civil-protection robot designed for tactical and law-enforcement use. It can carry a ballistic shield to provide mobile cover, extract wounded people from danger zones, and perform reconnaissance in active-threat or hazardous situations, keeping responders out of the line of fire.

name: Sojourner
desc: First wheeled vehicle to operate on another planet. Microwave-oven-sized six-wheeled rover delivered to Mars by the Mars Pathfinder mission in July 1997. Operated for 83 sols (12x its 7-sol design life), traveling 100 meters and returning 550 images plus chemical analyses of 16 rock and soil targets. Named after abolitionist Sojourner Truth.
cameras: 3 cameras: 2x front B&W stereo, 1x rear color (484x768 pixels)
also_known_as: Microrover Flight Experiment (MFEX), Mars Pathfinder Rover
actuator_type: Brushed DC motors with rocker-bogie suspension

name: Spirit (MER-A)
desc: First of NASA's twin Mars Exploration Rovers. Landed at Gusev Crater on 4 January 2004 with a 90-sol design life. Operated for 2,210 sols (over 6 years), traveled 7.73 km, and discovered evidence of past hydrothermal activity. Got stuck in soft soil in 2009 and continued as a stationary platform until last contact in March 2010.
cameras: 9 cameras: Pancam (stereo), Navcam (stereo), 4 Hazcams, Microscopic Imager
also_known_as: Mars Exploration Rover A, MER-A, Spirit Rover
actuator_type: Brushed DC motors with planetary gears, rocker-bogie suspension

name: Opportunity (MER-B)
desc: Twin of Spirit (MER-B). Landed at Meridiani Planum on 25 January 2004 and operated for 5,352 sols (over 14 years), traveling a record 45.16 km — the longest off-Earth drive in history. Discovered the first definitive evidence of past liquid water on Mars. Lost contact during a global dust storm in June 2018; mission officially ended February 2019.
cameras: 9 cameras: Pancam (stereo), Navcam (stereo), 4 Hazcams, Microscopic Imager
also_known_as: Mars Exploration Rover B, MER-B, Oppy
actuator_type: Brushed DC motors with planetary gears, rocker-bogie suspension

name: Curiosity
desc: Car-sized nuclear-powered rover, the heart of NASA's Mars Science Laboratory (MSL) mission. Landed in Gale Crater on 6 August 2012 using the novel Sky Crane delivery system. Still operational after 13+ years, has traversed over 35 km exploring Mount Sharp's sedimentary layers. Confirmed Mars once had habitable freshwater lake environments and detected complex organic molecules.
cameras: 17 cameras total: Mastcam stereo, Navcam stereo, 8 Hazcams, MAHLI hand lens, MARDI descent imager, ChemCam Remote Micro-Imager
actuator_type: Brushless DC motors, rocker-bogie suspension with 6 independently driven wheels
payload_instruments: Sample Analysis at Mars (SAM) — gas chromatograph + mass spectrometer + tunable laser spectrometer

name: Perseverance
desc: Largest, most advanced rover ever sent to Mars. Landed in Jezero Crater on 18 February 2021. Built on Curiosity heritage with improved wheels, autonomous navigation, and a sample caching system that collects rock cores for future Mars Sample Return. Deployed the Ingenuity helicopter and produced the first oxygen on Mars via MOXIE. Carries 7 advanced instruments and 23 cameras.
cameras: 23 cameras: Mastcam-Z stereo, Navcams stereo, 6 Hazcams, SHERLOC WATSON, PIXL camera, sampling cameras, Entry/Descent/Landing cameras
actuator_type: Brushless DC motors, redesigned rigid wheels with cleat patterns
payload_instruments: Scanning Habitable Environments with Raman & Luminescence for Organics & Chemicals (SHERLOC)
Mars Oxygen In-Situ Resource Utilization Experiment (MOXIE)
Radar Imager for Mars subsurface experiment (RIMFAX)

name: Ingenuity
desc: First aircraft to achieve powered, controlled flight on another planet. Small autonomous coaxial-rotor helicopter delivered to Mars by Perseverance in February 2021. Designed for just 5 flights and 30 sols; ultimately completed 72 flights covering 17 km over nearly 3 years before sustaining rotor blade damage in January 2024. Famously powered by a Qualcomm Snapdragon 801 (commercial smartphone chip).
cameras: Navigation camera (B&W) + Return to Earth (RTE) color camera
actuator_type: Coaxial counter-rotating rotors (2x 1.2 m), 2400 RPM

name: Lunokhod 1
desc: First remote-controlled robotic rover to land on another world. Soviet 8-wheeled lunar rover delivered by Luna 17 on 17 November 1970. Operated for 322 Earth days across 11 lunar days, traveled 10.54 km, and returned 20,000+ TV pictures and 200+ panoramas before its RTG depleted. Discovered in 2010 by NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter.
actuator_type: 8 independent wheel motors with springs (no suspension)
payload_instruments: TV cameras (low frame rate, 1 per few seconds)
power_source: Solar array on hinged lid + Polonium-210 RTG (night heating)

name: Lunokhod 2
desc: Second Soviet lunar rover, delivered by Luna 21 on 15 January 1973. Improved on Lunokhod 1 with better cameras, faster ground-control updates, and traveled 39 km (long held the all-time off-Earth distance record until surpassed by Opportunity in 2014). Overheated and failed in May 1973 after picking up lunar dust on its solar panels.
rtos: Teleoperation with improved 3.2-second TV update rate
actuator_type: 8 independent wheel motors
power_source: Solar array on hinged lid + Polonium-210 RTG (night heating)

name: Yutu
desc: First Chinese lunar rover, deployed from the Chang'e 3 lander on 15 December 2013 — the first soft landing on the Moon since 1976. Suffered a mechanical failure preventing further mobility after 114 m of traverse, but continued returning scientific data from its stationary position for 31 months. Named 'Yutu' (Jade Rabbit) after the lunar companion of Chang'e in Chinese mythology.
also_known_as: 玉兔, Jade Rabbit, Chang'e 3 Rover
actuator_type: 6 independently driven wheels with rocker suspension
power_source: Solar array + RHU (radioisotope heater) for lunar night

name: Yutu-2
desc: First spacecraft to operate on the far side of the Moon. Deployed from the Chang'e 4 lander on 3 January 2019 at Von Kármán crater. Still operational and holds the record for longest-operating lunar rover ever. Communicates with Earth via the Queqiao L2 relay satellite. Has discovered unusual 'gel-like' substances and significantly advanced understanding of the lunar far side.
also_known_as: 玉兔二号, Jade Rabbit 2, Chang'e 4 Rover
chipset: Chinese SPARC V8 rad-hardened (improved over Yutu)
actuator_type: 6 independently driven wheels with rocker suspension
payload_instruments: Advanced Small Analyzer for Neutrals (ASAN, Swedish-supplied)

name: Pragyan
desc: First Indian lunar rover and the first rover ever to operate near the lunar south pole. Deployed from the Vikram lander on 23 August 2023. Operated for 12 days (one lunar day) traversing 101.4 m before lunar night ended its mission. Could not be revived afterward but completed all mission objectives, including confirming the presence of sulfur and oxygen in the south polar regolith.
actuator_type: 6 independently driven wheels with rocker-bogie
target_body: Moon (south polar region, Statio Shiv Shakti)
mission_type: Lunar south pole mobile geology rover

name: Zhurong
desc: China's first Mars rover, part of the Tianwen-1 mission. Deployed from the Tianwen-1 lander at Utopia Planitia on 22 May 2021, making China the second nation to successfully operate a rover on Mars. Operated for 358 sols and traveled 1.921 km before entering hibernation in May 2022; has not awoken from hibernation since. Named after the Chinese god of fire.
cameras: Navigation/Terrain Cameras (NaTeCam stereo), Multispectral Camera (MSCam), Hazard avoidance cameras
actuator_type: Active suspension with 6 independently driven wheels (can crab-walk)
mission_status: Decommissioned (last contact May 2022, hibernation never ended)
payload_instruments: Mars Surface Composition Detector (MarSCoDe) — LIBS spectrometer

name: SLIM
desc: Smart Lander for Investigating Moon. Demonstrated high-precision (100m) lunar landing on 19 January 2024, making Japan the fifth nation to soft-land on the Moon. Landed on its side after one of two main engines lost thrust, but achieved its primary precision-landing technology demonstration goal. Deployed two micro-rovers LEV-1 and LEV-2 (SORA-Q) before touchdown.
also_known_as: Smart Lander for Investigating Moon, Moon Sniper

name: LEV-1
desc: Lunar Excursion Vehicle 1. Small hopping/jumping micro-rover deployed by SLIM just before touchdown on 19 January 2024. Uses leaf-spring legs to hop across the lunar surface. Operated autonomously without ground commands, communicating with Earth directly via UHF antenna — a first for a lunar surface vehicle.
actuator_type: Leaf-spring hopping mechanism + reaction wheels

name: LEV-2 (SORA-Q)
desc: Lunar Excursion Vehicle 2, also known as SORA-Q. Baseball-sized transformable spherical robot co-developed with toy maker Tomy. Deployed from SLIM on 19 January 2024 and transformed from a sphere into a two-wheeled vehicle on the lunar surface. Returned the iconic image of SLIM resting on its side on the Moon. World's smallest lunar rover.
also_known_as: SORA-Q, ソラキュー, Transformable Lunar Robot
operating_agency: JAXA / Takara Tomy / Sony / Doshisha University
actuator_type: Two transformable wheel/hemisphere shells

name: Viking 1 Lander
desc: First spacecraft to successfully soft-land on Mars and complete its mission. Equipped with a 3-meter robotic surface sampler arm that scooped Martian soil into onboard biology, chemistry, and meteorology instruments. Operated for over 6 years on the surface, returning more than 4,500 images and groundbreaking data that defined Mars science for decades.
actuator_type: Electric motors
cameras: Twin 360° cylindrical scan cameras with 6 selectable spectral filters
chipset: Honeywell GCSC (General-purpose Computer for Spacecraft Control)
rtos: Custom Viking Lander Flight Program (FORTRAN compiled to GCSC machine code)
storage_type: Tape recorder (40 MB total per lander)

name: Viking 2 Lander
desc: Second Viking lander, touched down at Utopia Planitia in September 1976. Identical hardware to Viking 1 with a 3-meter robotic surface sampler arm. Operated for nearly 4 years before battery failure. Landed at an 8.2° tilt with one leg on a rock after radar misidentification caused thrusters to fire briefly extra at touchdown.
also_known_as: Viking Lander 2, Gerald Soffen Memorial Station
actuator_type: Electric motors
cameras: Twin 360° cylindrical scan cameras with 6 selectable spectral filters
chipset: Honeywell GCSC (General-purpose Computer for Spacecraft Control)
storage_type: Tape recorder (40 MB total per lander)

name: Phoenix
desc: Polar Mars lander equipped with a 2.35 m robotic arm capable of digging trenches to access subsurface water ice. Confirmed the presence of water ice on Mars and detected perchlorates in the soil. Built on Mars Surveyor 2001 spare hardware. Operated for 157 sols (5 months) at 68°N latitude before the Martian winter ended its mission.
also_known_as: Phoenix Mars Lander, Phoenix Mars Mission
actuator_type: Brushed DC motors with planetary gearheads
cameras: Surface Stereo Imager (2 cameras), Robotic Arm Camera, MARDI descent imager

name: InSight
desc: Interior Exploration using Seismic Investigations, Geodesy and Heat Transport. Stationary Mars lander built on the Phoenix design with larger solar panels. Equipped with a robotic instrument deployment arm that placed a French-built seismometer (SEIS) and a German-built self-hammering heat probe (HP3 'mole') on the surface. Detected over 1,300 marsquakes and revealed Mars's interior structure before being decommissioned due to dust buildup on solar panels.
also_known_as: Interior Exploration using Seismic Investigations, GEMS, Discovery 12
actuator_type: Brushed DC motors with harmonic drives
payload_instruments: Heat Flow and Physical Properties Package (HP3)
cameras: Instrument Deployment Camera (IDC, color), Instrument Context Camera (ICC, fisheye)

name: Vikram
desc: Chandrayaan-3 lunar lander, named after Vikram Sarabhai. Soft-landed near the lunar south pole at Statio Shiv Shakti on 23 August 2023, making India the fourth nation to achieve a soft Moon landing and the first to land in the south polar region. Deployed the Pragyan rover. Improved design from failed Chandrayaan-2 Vikram with stronger legs and four (not five) throttlable engines.
chipset: ISRO Vikram-1601 PROM SoC (rad-hardened, indigenously developed)

name: Tianwen-1 Lander
desc: China's Tianwen-1 lander (2021) delivered the Zhurong rover to Utopia Planitia on Mars, making China the second nation to operate a rover on the Martian surface. It used a combination of aeroshell, parachute and retro-propulsion with hazard-avoidance hovering for landing.
also_known_as: Tianwen 1 Entry Descent and Landing System
power_source: Battery (transferred power to rover then dormant)
chipset: Chinese SPARC V8 rad-hardened processor (classified specifics)

name: Huygens
desc: First and only spacecraft to land on a moon in the outer solar system. Released from the Cassini orbiter and parachuted to the surface of Saturn's moon Titan on 14 January 2005, returning unprecedented surface images and atmospheric data for 90 minutes after touchdown. Holds the record for furthest landing ever (1.4 billion km from Earth) and only landing on a moon other than Earth's.

name: Philae
desc: First spacecraft to soft-land on a comet. Released by the Rosetta orbiter onto Comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko on 12 November 2014. Harpoons failed to fire on landing, causing Philae to bounce twice and come to rest in a shadowed location ~1 km from intended site. Operated intermittently on battery power for ~60 hours before going silent; briefly re-established contact in mid-2015.

name: Hayabusa
desc: World's first asteroid sample return mission. Rendezvoused with near-Earth asteroid 25143 Itokawa in 2005, performed two touch-and-go sampling attempts despite numerous technical failures, and returned a small sample (~1500 dust particles) to Earth in 2010. Mission was nearly lost multiple times — fuel leak, ion engine failures, communication blackouts — but survived through ingenious recovery operations.
power_source: Solar array + Li-ion battery + 4 xenon ion thrusters

name: Hayabusa 2
desc: Successor to Hayabusa, dramatically more successful. Rendezvoused with asteroid 162173 Ryugu in 2018, deployed multiple landers (MINERVA-II-1A/1B rovers and MASCOT), created an artificial crater with a 2.5 kg copper impactor, and returned 5.4 g of pristine samples to Earth on 6 December 2020. Now on an extended mission to asteroid 1998 KY26, arriving 2031.
mission_type: Asteroid sample return with multiple landers
power_source: Solar array + Li-ion battery + ion thrusters (10x more powerful than Hayabusa)

name: OSIRIS-REx / OSIRIS-APEX
desc: Origins, Spectral Interpretation, Resource Identification, and Security - Regolith Explorer. Collected 121.6 g of samples from asteroid 101955 Bennu using its TAGSAM (Touch-and-Go Sample Acquisition Mechanism) arm and returned them to Earth in September 2023 — the largest asteroid sample ever returned. Renamed OSIRIS-APEX for an extended mission to asteroid 99942 Apophis, arriving April 2029 just after Apophis's close Earth flyby.
payload_instruments: OSIRIS-REx Camera Suite (OCAMS): PolyCam, MapCam, SamCam

name: Stardust
desc: First spacecraft to return samples from a comet. Flew through the coma of Comet 81P/Wild 2 in January 2004 at 6.1 km/s, collecting particles in an aerogel collector, and returned the sample capsule to Earth in January 2006. Recovered particles included a new mineral, glycine (amino acid), and pre-solar grains. Later repurposed as Stardust-NExT for a flyby of Comet 9P/Tempel 1 in 2011.

name: MINERVA-II-1A (Rover 1A)
desc: JAXA's MINERVA-II-1A (Rover-1A) was one of two tiny hopping rovers deployed from Hayabusa2 onto asteroid Ryugu in 2018 - the first rovers to successfully operate on an asteroid surface. It moved by hopping in the micro-gravity and returned surface images.
actuator_type: Internal torquer / flywheel (no wheels)

name: MINERVA-II-1B (Rover 1B / OWL)
desc: JAXA's MINERVA-II-1B (Rover-1B) was the second of the paired hopping rovers released from Hayabusa2 onto asteroid Ryugu in 2018, working alongside Rover-1A to image the surface and demonstrate hopping mobility in extremely low gravity.
actuator_type: Internal torquer / flywheel

name: MASCOT
desc: Mobile Asteroid Surface Scout. Shoebox-sized lander built by the German Aerospace Center (DLR) and France's CNES, deployed by Hayabusa 2 onto asteroid Ryugu on 3 October 2018. Hopped once to reposition itself using an internal swing arm and operated for 17 hours on primary battery power, exceeding its 16-hour design lifetime. Returned data on Ryugu's surface composition.
actuator_type: Internal swing arm (for hopping)

name: Canadarm (SRMS)
desc: Shuttle Remote Manipulator System (SRMS). The 15.2 m, 6-DOF robotic arm operated on all 90 Space Shuttle missions from 1981 to 2011, deploying and retrieving payloads including the Hubble Space Telescope. Established Canadian leadership in space robotics. Built by Spar Aerospace (now MDA), it could handle payloads up to 29,000 kg in microgravity but only 90 kg in Earth's gravity.
also_known_as: SRMS, Shuttle Remote Manipulator System, RMS
actuator_type: Brushed DC motors with epicyclic gear reduction
mission_type: Robotic arm for payload deployment and retrieval
payload_instruments: Standard End Effector (SEE) for grapple fixtures

name: Canadarm2 (SSRMS)
desc: Space Station Remote Manipulator System (SSRMS). 17.6 m, 7-DOF arm installed on the ISS in 2001. Capable of 'walking' along the station by attaching either end to a base point. Routinely captures visiting cargo spacecraft including SpaceX Dragon and Northrop Grumman Cygnus, and assists astronauts during spacewalks. Built by MDA. Still operational after 25 years.
also_known_as: SSRMS, Space Station Remote Manipulator System
actuator_type: Brushless DC motors with redundant windings
mission_type: Mobile robotic arm with hand-over-hand walking

name: Dextre (SPDM)
desc: Special Purpose Dexterous Manipulator (SPDM). Two-armed dexterous robot installed on the ISS in 2008, designed to perform precise maintenance tasks that previously required spacewalks. Each arm has 7 DOF. Attaches to the end of Canadarm2 or directly to the station structure. Has performed satellite refueling demonstrations (RRM) and pump module replacements.
also_known_as: SPDM, Special Purpose Dexterous Manipulator, Canada Hand
actuator_type: Brushless DC motors
payload_instruments: Tool changeout mechanism (ORU/Tool Changeout Mechanism, OTCM)

name: JEMRMS
desc: Japanese Experiment Module Remote Manipulator System. Two-part robotic arm (Main Arm 10 m + Small Fine Arm 2.2 m) attached to the Kibo module of the ISS. Handles external payloads on the Kibo Exposed Facility. The Main Arm can position payloads with 50 mm accuracy; the Small Fine Arm achieves 10 mm precision for delicate experiments.
also_known_as: Japanese Experiment Module Remote Manipulator System, Kibo Arm
actuator_type: Brushless DC motors
payload_instruments: End effector for Kibo exposed facility payload exchange
Small Fine Arm (SFA) for precision tasks

name: European Robotic Arm (ERA)
desc: 11.3 m symmetrical 7-DOF arm with end effectors at both ends, allowing it to 'walk' hand-over-hand around the Russian segment of the ISS. Launched on the Nauka module in July 2021 and operational since 2022 after commissioning spacewalks. Built by Airbus Defence and Space Netherlands. Designed for cosmonaut EVA support and external payload handling.
actuator_type: Brushless DC motors
payload_instruments: Symmetric end effectors x2 with grapple capability

name: Astrobee Honey
desc: One of three free-flying autonomous robots on the ISS. 32 cm cube uses 6 electric impeller fans for propulsion in microgravity, runs Android-based software on a Snapdragon SoC, and serves as a platform for researchers to test guest-science payloads. Honey is the yellow one of the trio; introduced for visual identification.
actuator_type: 6 electric impeller fans for propulsion

name: Astrobee Queen
desc: Second of three Astrobee free-flying robots on the ISS. Identical hardware to Honey and Bumble (the blue one of the trio), used for autonomous navigation research, payload transport, and remote inspection inside the station. Queen was the first Astrobee to fly fully in 2019.
actuator_type: 6 electric impeller fans

name: Astrobee Bumble
desc: Third of three Astrobee free-flying robots on the ISS. The blue/yellow striped one of the trio. Used for autonomous flight research, environmental monitoring, and supporting astronaut activities through teleoperation or scripted behaviors. Replaced an earlier-generation robot called SPHERES.
actuator_type: 6 electric impeller fans

name: CIMON
desc: Crew Interactive Mobile Companion. Spherical AI assistant developed by Airbus and IBM (Watson) for DLR. Operated briefly on the ISS in 2018, designed to assist astronauts with experiments and provide voice-controlled information retrieval. Used 14 internal impellers for free-flight in microgravity. Pioneered AI-driven crew companionship in space.
actuator_type: 14 internal impellers (fans)

name: CIMON-2
desc: Second-generation Crew Interactive Mobile Companion. Improved AI emotional sensitivity (using Watson Tone Analyzer), longer battery life, and more robust flight capability than CIMON. Operated on the ISS from 2019 with multiple successful astronaut interaction sessions including with ESA astronaut Luca Parmitano.
actuator_type: 14 internal impellers (fans)

name: Double 3
desc: The third-generation Double Robotics mobile telepresence robot. Introduced dual cameras with 13-megapixel stills and 150° wide-angle obstacle avoidance, plus a beamforming microphone array. Superseded by Double 4 in late 2024.

name: Double 4
desc: Fourth-generation flagship mobile telepresence robot from Double Robotics, unveiled November 2024. Improved obstacle avoidance, sturdier base for uneven floors, and seamless integration with Zoom, Microsoft Teams and Google Meet.
secondary_camera: Floor camera with HDR night vision

name: Double 2
desc: The robot that defined the consumer telepresence category. Self-balancing two-wheel base with iPad as the screen and brain, allowing remote workers to attend meetings, walk hallways, and tour facilities from anywhere.

name: BeamPro
desc: Enterprise telepresence robot that defined the high-end remote-presence category. Used widely in tech-company offices including by Edward Snowden remotely. Original Suitable Technologies wound down in 2020; brand revived with Beam Pro 3 in 2025.

name: Beam Pro 3
desc: Third-generation Beam Pro announced May 2025 as Suitable Technologies' return to the market. Features higher-resolution 4K video, improved battery life, and enhanced enterprise management tools.

name: Ohmni Supercam
desc: OhmniLabs' next-generation flagship launched March 2025, featuring ultra-high-resolution 4K camera and AI-powered auto-framing for healthcare, enterprise collaboration, and distance learning.

name: Ohmni
desc: OhmniLabs' original consumer-friendly mobile telepresence robot. Lightweight three-wheel design with HD video and tilt-screen mechanism for natural eye contact. Widely deployed in healthcare and remote-work contexts.

name: Temi
desc: Autonomous mobile robot blending telepresence with personal-assistant functionality. Uses 3D vision and LiDAR for autonomous navigation, can follow users, dock automatically, and deliver items between rooms.
languages_spoken: English, Mandarin, Hebrew, Spanish, French, German, Japanese, Arabic

name: Temi Pro
desc: Business-focused Temi launched July 2024 with enhanced autonomy, 4K camera, and improved navigation. Targeted at retail, healthcare, hospitality, and corporate deployments where reliability and fleet management matter.

name: Ava Telepresence
desc: Enterprise-grade autonomous telepresence robot built on Ava Robotics' navigation platform (spun out from iRobot). Self-navigates to meeting rooms, integrates with Cisco Webex and Microsoft Teams, and added AI environmental sensors via Cisco partnership in 2025.

name: VGo
desc: One of the earliest commercial telepresence robots. Widely deployed in K-12 schools to let homebound students attend classes, and in hospitals for remote patient consultations. Acquired by Vecna Technologies in 2015.

name: Anybots QB
desc: One of the first commercial telepresence robots. Self-balancing two-wheel design predated Double Robotics. Anybots discontinued the QB by 2014 before relaunching as Anybots 2.0 with industrial focus.

name: Anybots QX
desc: Industrial-focused telepresence robot completing beta testing in September 2024 with commercial launch Q2 2025. Ruggedized for remote industrial inspections in manufacturing and oil & gas, with thermal imaging and multi-terrain mobility.

name: Giraff
desc: Eldercare-focused telepresence robot for the European market. Used in numerous EU-funded research projects on independent living for older adults. Brand later transitioned to Camanio Care.

name: Teladoc InTouch Lite
desc: Clinical-grade telepresence robot for hospital deployments. Originally from InTouch Health (acquired by Teladoc in 2020 for $600M), used in stroke care, ICU consultations, and tele-ICU programs across major hospital networks worldwide.

name: Kubi
desc: Tabletop telepresence robot — a pan/tilt cradle for an iPad. Let remote participants look around a meeting room rather than being stuck with a fixed laptop view. Acquired by Xandex in 2017.

name: MantaroBot
desc: US-made mobile telepresence platform with customizable hardware configurations. Used by enterprise and government customers including military training and remote inspection applications.

name: PadBot U1
desc: Budget consumer mobile telepresence robot from Chinese manufacturer Inbot Technology. Mounted a tablet on a self-balancing base, targeting small-business and personal use cases at a fraction of premium-brand pricing.

name: Texai
desc: Research telepresence prototype from Willow Garage (also the birthplace of ROS and PR2). Internal deployment at Willow Garage allowed remote employees to be present in the office. Never sold commercially but influenced the entire category.

name: PARO
desc: The original therapeutic social robot. Modeled on a baby harp seal, PARO is the longest-deployed eldercare robot worldwide with documented clinical benefits for dementia patients — reducing agitation and improving mood. FDA-cleared as a Class 2 medical device since 2009.
manufacturer_history: AIST (National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology), Japan. Co-leads the Humanoid Robotics Project (HRP / 'Promet') with Kawada Industries + Kawasaki, sponsored by METI/NEDO. HRP lineage: HRP-1 (from Honda P3) → HRP-2 (can stand up from lying) → HRP-3 → HRP-4 → HRP-4C (female) → HRP-5P (2018, power tools + drywall handling, most autonomous).

raw_specs.maker: AIST (Japan) + Kawada + Kawasaki — Humanoid Robotics Project (HRP/Promet)

name: ElliQ 3
desc: Tabletop AI companion designed as a proactive engagement partner for older adults living alone. Deployed by New York State Office for the Aging and other US agency programs. Initiates conversations, sets medication reminders, leads cognitive exercises, and connects family via video call.
pilot_customers: NY State Office for the Aging

name: Moxie
desc: Companion robot for children ages 5-10 developed by Embodied (founded by former iRobot CTO Paolo Pirjanian). Used conversational AI and expressive animations to help kids develop emotional and social skills. Embodied wound down operations in late 2024 but units remain in active use.

name: Miko 3
desc: AI-powered conversational companion for children ages 5-10 combining play and STEM education. Indian unicorn valued at $550M with strong global sales. Includes built-in tablet face, voice interaction, and content library covering math, science, reading.

name: Miko Mini
desc: Compact, lower-cost sibling to Miko 3. Same conversational AI but in a static tabletop form. Targets gift-buyer parents at the sub-$150 price point and has been a strong holiday seller in US/UK markets.

name: Lovot
desc: Non-verbal emotional companion robot designed by ex-Pepper engineer Kaname Hayashi. Recognizes family members, responds to touch and voice, exhibits learned attachment behaviors. Wildly popular in Japan — sold tens of thousands of units despite the high price point.
shell_material: Soft fabric outer body, ABS frame

name: Jibo
desc: The world's first commercial social robot for the home. Developed by MIT Media Lab's Cynthia Breazeal. Sold from 2017-2018, NTT Disruption acquired remnants in 2020. Cult following — its 'final goodbye' update in 2019 became a viral cultural moment about emotional bonds with robots.

name: Vector 2.0
desc: Revived version of the original Anki Vector after Digital Dream Labs acquired the IP in 2020. Compact desktop companion with personality, voice interaction, Alexa integration, and local processing for privacy.

name: Cozmo
desc: Tabletop personality robot from Anki with expressive facial animations and code-with-Cozmo programming feature. Anki shut down in 2019. Massively influential in the AI-personality category — many of today's social bots draw lineage from Cozmo's design language.

name: Loona
desc: Expressive smart pet robot from Shenzhen-based KEYi Tech. Combines lifelike animations, voice recognition, and emotion-detection AI. Successfully Kickstarted in 2022 raising over $4M, has shipped to 60+ countries.

name: Eilik
desc: Affordable desktop personality robot that went viral via TikTok. Two units can interact and chat with each other. No app, no subscription, no internet required — runs offline with built-in personality scripts.

name: Qoobo
desc: Therapeutic robotic cushion with a moving tail. No face, no voice — just a tail that responds to touch like a cat. Designed for people who can't keep pets (apartments, allergies, eldercare). Won multiple design awards including Red Dot.

name: Hyodol
desc: ChatGPT-powered companion doll deployed at scale in South Korea. Over 12,000 units distributed by Korean municipal governments to elderly living alone. Tracks medication, provides conversation, alerts emergency contacts when issues arise.

name: Abi
desc: AI-powered eldercare companion robot from Melbourne-based Andromeda Robotics. Raised $17M in March 2026 to expand into the US senior care market. Deployed across Australian aged-care homes with focus on cognitive engagement and dignified assistance.

name: Ryan
desc: Tabletop social robot from DreamFace Technologies (University of Denver spin-off) featuring an animated face projected onto a translucent 3D head. Used in dementia care research and clinical settings — focused on engaging conversations with cognitively impaired adults.

name: Buddy
desc: Family-oriented social robot from French startup Blue Frog Robotics. Funded via Indiegogo, shipped 2018. Designed to be a household assistant, security monitor, and child companion. Company restructured in 2024 ending consumer sales.

name: Kuri
desc: Family home companion from Mayfield Robotics (a Bosch subsidiary). Cute design with autonomous navigation, no face screen — communicated entirely through eye animations and chirps. Bosch shut down Mayfield in 2018 before mass shipping. All customer deposits were refunded.

name: BDX Droid
desc: Disney's autonomous interactive Star Wars droid character — short for 'Bipedal Dynamic Experiment.' Variants include OSKAR-7 (orange), BESH-27 (blue), GREK-17 (green), Red. Won the 2025 Thea Award for Technical Innovation. Roams Galaxy's Edge at Disneyland, Disney World, Tokyo Disneyland, Disneyland Paris and Shanghai Disneyland. Debuts on screen in The Mandalorian and Grogu (May 2026). Patent filed October 2023 as 'walking robots.'
actuator_type: Custom servo-driven (~$7,500 actuator package)
ai_model: Disney Research autonomous behavior model (RL + Imitation)

name: Project Kiwi (Baby Groot)
desc: Free-walking autonomous Baby Groot character developed by Disney Imagineering as a milestone in expressive character robotics. Pint-sized humanoid with accurately rendered face/hands/feet, distressed red flight suit, expressive eye contact. The Project Kiwi platform later evolved into the BDX droid program. Stages controlled meet-and-greet appearances.
actuator_type: Custom servo-driven

name: Walt Disney – A Magical Life
desc: Audio-Animatronic figure of Walt Disney himself, opened July 17 2025 at Disneyland California for the park's 70th anniversary. Plays in rotation with Great Moments with Mr. Lincoln (1964). 17-minute stage show in the Main Street, USA section. Controversial — Walt's granddaughter Joanna Miller publicly opposed the robot likeness, calling it 'dehumanizing.'
actuator_type: Pneumatic + servo
pilot_customers: Disneyland Park, Main Street USA (Disneyland Opera House)

name: ADAM
desc: Dual-armed AI-powered bartender (Automated Dual Arm Mixologist) from NASDAQ-listed Richtech Robotics. Debuted at CES 2024. First robot bartender permanently stationed at a major league sports venue (Texas Rangers Globe Life Field, 2024). Now serving at T-Mobile Arena NHL games. 23-drink menu, NSF certified for food service.
form_factor: Dual-arm robotic torso on counter base
actuator_type: Electric (2x Richtech ARM modules)
pilot_customers: T-Mobile Arena Las Vegas (NHL Golden Knights)

name: Makr Shakr (Toni)
desc: Two-armed robotic bartender installation co-designed with MIT and Pentagram design studio. Permanently installed on Royal Caribbean's Quantum-class cruise ships, airports, hotels and event spaces worldwide. Compatto model adds coffee; Veloce model can make up to 250 drinks per hour. Pioneered the robotic bartender category.
actuator_type: Electric (Kuka industrial arms)

name: Kuratas
desc: Pilot-operated 4-meter mecha from Japanese artist Kogoro Kurata. Famous for the 2017 international mecha duel against MegaBots Inc.'s Eagle Prime (USA). Available for purchase or rental for events. Combines theatrical scale with a working piloted cockpit. Controlled via Kinect-style motion or smartphone.
actuator_type: Diesel-powered, four-wheeled rolling base, hydraulic arms; V-Sido control system (cockpit or smartphone piloting)
use_cases: The original commercial pilotable mecha (from ~US.35 million)
Fought MegaBots in the 2017 USA-vs-Japan giant robot duel

name: Stickboy (Compressorhead drummer)
desc: Four-armed pneumatic drummer in the world's first robotic heavy metal band Compressorhead. Built by German engineers from steel auto parts. Has played live across Europe and Australia, opened for Black Sabbath at Wacken Open Air 2016. The full band includes Bones (bass), Fingers (guitar), and Hellga (vocals).
actuator_type: Pneumatic

name: Z-Machines
desc: Japanese all-robot band consisting of MACH (78-finger guitarist), ASHURA (22-arm drummer), and COSMO (laser keyboardist). Created by Naofumi Yonetsuka (Tokyo University), performed at SXSW 2013 and Tokyo. Squarepusher composed 'Music for Robots' EP specifically for them in 2014. Project paused after 2015.
actuator_type: Electric servo

name: Blue (Newton-trained BDX)

desc: The Conga 9990 AI is a robot vacuum and mop from Cecotec with an auto-empty dock that autonomously navigates and cleans home floors, returning to its dock to recharge.

name: S10 Pro
desc: A vacuum-and-mop robot notable for its hidden trinocular LiDAR — the sensors are embedded flush in the body instead of a top turret, giving an ultra-slim 8.5 cm profile that reaches under low furniture. A Nidec brushless motor delivers up to 3,300 Pa across four power modes, with dToF 3D obstacle avoidance recognising 100+ object types, an electronic 520 mL water tank with active mop pressure, and ultrasonic carpet detection. The Pro variant adds an auto-empty base.

name: S9
desc: A vacuum-and-mop robot with a dual-eye navigation system pairing a spinning LiDAR turret with an ultrasonic module across a 25-sensor suite for accurate straight-line mapping. Delivers 2,650 Pa suction with automatic carpet boost, stores up to 10 floor maps, and — unusually — ships with a dedicated RF remote control alongside app and voice control. A 5,200 mAh battery gives up to ~180 minutes of runtime with recharge-and-resume.

name: Scuba X1
desc: The Scuba X1 is a robotic pool cleaner from Aiper that autonomously scrubs and vacuums pool floors, walls and waterline, filtering debris without a hose or pump connection.

name: Seagull 2000 (SE)
desc: A mid-range cordless robotic pool cleaner in Aiper's Seagull line, adding wall-climbing to the floor-cleaning of the entry Seagull models. Uses a dual-motor drive with WavePath-style path planning and a rechargeable battery, cleaning pool floors and walls without a cord or booster pump. Automatically parks near the pool edge when the battery runs low.
use_cases: Above-ground and in-ground pool cleaning (floor + walls)

name: Orca 2000
desc: A corded robotic pool cleaner in Aiper's Orca line for in-ground pools, positioned as a high-value wall-climbing cleaner. A 200 W triple-axis drive motor with 4-wheel drive and dual PVC roller brushes scrubs and vacuums the floor, walls and up to the waterline, cleaning pools up to ~2,153 sq ft in about two hours. A 60 ft tangle-free floating cord with a built-in swivel prevents entanglement, and a dedicated RF remote gives stable manual steering (rather than unreliable outdoor Wi-Fi/Bluetooth). Multi-layer filtration ships with 100/200/400-micron filter bags to target different debris sizes.
use_cases: In-ground pools up to ~2,153 sq ft

name: yeedi Cube Pro
desc: Upgraded successor to the yeedi Cube (Cube Pro S1) - all-in-one vacuum + mop with 5,100Pa suction, self-empty + self-wash + self-dry station, a 1L 'mega' top water tank covering ~200 m2, and rapid hot-air mop drying. Up to 180min runtime.

name: NoMo Q11
desc: A self-emptying 3-in-1 vacuum-mop with a distinctive retro-futuristic design. Hidden dToF laser LiDAR (built into the body rather than a turret) keeps it just 8.7 cm tall for under-furniture access, paired with structured-light 3D AI obstacle avoidance. Up to 4,000 Pa suction with automatic carpet boost, and a boot-shaped dock that vacuums the robot's bin into a 2.5 L bag for ~30 days hands-free.

name: Qrevo Edge
desc: The Roborock Qrevo Edge (2024) raises suction to 18,500 Pa HyperForce with a DuoDivide anti-tangle brush and adds FlexiArm extending mops and side brush for true edge-to-edge coverage. Dual spinning pads, 75 C hot-water mop wash and warm-air drying in the dock, PreciSense LiDAR plus Reactive AI obstacle recognition.

name: L9000
desc: A value LiDAR vacuum-and-mop combo and the flagship of budget brand Tikom (launched 2021). Uses 360° LDS laser navigation to build accurate maps and save up to five floor plans, delivers 4,000 Pa suction with automatic carpet boost to Max, and mops via an electronically controlled pump with three water levels. Controlled through the Tuya-based app with Alexa and Google voice support and up to 14 no-go zones. A Plus variant adds a 2.5 L self-empty dock.

name: Q6 Pro
desc: A value self-emptying vacuum-and-mop with LDS laser navigation and a 26-sensor suite for detailed mapping and obstacle avoidance. Up to 4,000 Pa suction with automatic carpet boost (2,000 to 4,000 Pa), a 2-in-1 electric water tank and dustbin, and a large 4 L auto-empty station that clears the bin in ~20 seconds for up to ~70 days hands-free. A 5,200 mAh battery gives up to 250 minutes covering ~400 m².

name: S8 MaxV Ultra
desc: Roborock's S8 MaxV Ultra is the 2024 apex of the S8 line: 10,000 Pa HyperForce suction, a DuoRoller dual rubber brush, and a VibraRise 2.0 sonic mop scrubbing at 4,000 times/min that lifts 20 mm over carpet. Reactive AI 2.0 pairs 3D structured light with an RGB camera to recognise 73 object types, and the 8-in-1 RockDock Ultra auto-empties (~7 weeks), washes the mop in up to 60 C hot water, dries it, and refills the robot's 100 ml tank from a 4 L clean-water supply. 5,200 mAh battery, ~180 min runtime, ~300 m2 per charge.

name: Chang'e 3 Lander
desc: China's Chang'e 3 lander (2013) achieved the first soft lunar landing since 1976, touching down in Mare Imbrium and deploying the Yutu rover. It carried cameras, an extreme-ultraviolet telescope and ground-penetrating instruments, operating for years beyond its design life.

name: Chang'e 4 Lander
desc: China's Chang'e 4 lander (2019) made the first-ever soft landing on the far side of the Moon, in Von Karman crater, relaying data via the Queqiao relay satellite and deploying the Yutu-2 rover for the longest-running lunar surface mission.
payload_instruments: Biological Experiment Payload (carried cotton seeds — first plant grown on Moon)

name: Chang'e 5 Lander
desc: First lunar sample return mission since the Soviet Luna 24 in 1976. Landed in Mons Rümker region of Oceanus Procellarum on 1 December 2020, used a robotic arm and drill to collect 1.731 kg of lunar regolith, and launched it back to Earth via the ascent stage on 3 December. Samples were the youngest ever collected from the Moon (~2 billion years old), reshaping understanding of lunar volcanism.
mission_status: Decommissioned (ascent stage returned samples to Earth)
actuator_type: Brushless DC motors

name: VIPER
desc: Volatiles Investigating Polar Exploration Rover. Golf-cart-sized rover designed to search for water ice at the lunar south pole. Originally targeting a 2023 launch on Astrobotic's Griffin lander, then cancelled by NASA in July 2024 to cut costs, but revived in September 2025 with Blue Origin's Blue Moon Mark 1 as the new delivery vehicle. Will be the first rover specifically designed to operate in permanently shadowed lunar regions.
actuator_type: 4 independently steered wheels with active suspension
launch_vehicle: Blue Origin New Glenn (via Blue Moon Mark 1 lander)
power_source: Solar array + Li-ion battery (designed for cold lunar night survival)

name: Peregrine Mission One
desc: Astrobotic's Peregrine (Jan 2024) was a commercial CLPS lunar lander; a propellant leak after launch prevented a Moon landing and it was guided to re-enter Earth's atmosphere - a notable milestone attempt in commercial lunar robotics.
payload_instruments: 20 commercial and government payloads including 5 NASA CLPS instruments: Linear Energy Transfer Spectrometer (LETS)
outcome: Propellant leak after launch; controlled Earth re-entry (no landing)

name: Nova-C IM-1 (Odysseus)
desc: First US spacecraft to soft-land on the Moon since Apollo 17 in 1972, and first commercial soft landing in history. Landed near the lunar south pole at Malapert A crater on 22 February 2024 but tipped over on landing after a leg broke, limiting science operations. Most payloads remained functional. Used methalox propulsion — first to use it in deep space.
also_known_as: Odysseus, Odie, IM-1, CLPS Task Order 2-IM
target_body: Moon (Malapert A crater, south pole region)
payload_instruments: Stereo Cameras for Lunar Plume-Surface Studies (SCALPSS)
Plus 6 commercial: ILO-X telescope, EagleCam camera, etc.

name: Nova-C IM-2 (Athena)
desc: Intuitive Machines' second lunar lander mission, launched 27 February 2025. Touched down at Mons Mouton near the lunar south pole on 6 March 2025 but landed on its side inside a crater approximately 250 m from the intended site. Mission ended within a day due to inability to recharge solar panels. Carried the Micro-Nova Hopper, the MAPP rover, and PRIME-1 ice-drilling experiment.
also_known_as: Athena, IM-2, CLPS Task Order CP-11
mission_type: Commercial lunar lander (CLPS) with rover and hopper
payload_instruments: PRIME-1 (Polar Resources Ice Mining Experiment): TRIDENT drill + MSolo mass spectrometer

name: Blue Ghost Mission 1
desc: First fully successful commercial lunar landing in history. Landed upright in Mare Crisium near Mons Latreille on 2 March 2025, completing all primary mission objectives over 14 Earth days. Operated 10 NASA CLPS science payloads on the lunar surface. First mission to capture a GPS lock from the Moon and high-resolution video of a lunar sunset. Powered down for lunar night on 16 March 2025.
also_known_as: BGM1, Ghost Riders in the Sky, CLPS TO 19D
payload_instruments: 10 NASA CLPS payloads: Lunar GNSS Receiver Experiment (LuGRE)
Stereo Cameras for Lunar Plume-Surface Studies (SCALPSS)
Lunar Instrumentation for Subsurface Thermal Exploration with Rapidity (LISTER)

name: Hakuto-R Mission 1
desc: First commercial lunar landing attempt by a private Japanese company. Launched 11 December 2022, successfully reached lunar orbit, but crashed during landing attempt on 25 April 2023 due to an altitude sensor misreading caused by passing over the rim of Atlas Crater. Carried the UAE's Rashid rover and JAXA's transformable SORA-Q technology demonstrator (which was reflown on SLIM in 2024).
payload_instruments: Rashid rover (UAE Mohammed Bin Rashid Space Centre — first Arab Moon mission)
AI flight computer (Mission Control Space Services)

name: Hakuto-R Mission 2 (Resilience)
desc: ispace's Hakuto-R Mission 2 (Resilience, 2025) was a Japanese commercial lunar lander carrying the Tenacious micro-rover. Like Mission 1 (2023), it reached lunar orbit but did not achieve a successful soft landing, as ispace continues developing commercial cislunar transport.

name: Griffin Mission One
desc: Astrobotic's Griffin Mission 1 is a large commercial lunar lander developed under NASA's CLPS programme. Originally tasked with delivering NASA's VIPER rover (later removed by NASA), Griffin is one of the biggest US commercial landers, designed to carry substantial payloads to the lunar surface.
payload_instruments: VIPER mass simulator (replacing cancelled VIPER rover)

name: Int-Ball
desc: JEM Internal Ball Camera. Small spherical free-flying camera drone deployed inside Japan's Kibo module on the ISS in 2017. Designed to reduce the workload of astronauts who previously spent ~10% of their time on photo/video documentation. Diameter just 15 cm — could be deployed and recovered by hand. Operational until 2019.
also_known_as: JEM Internal Ball Camera, JEM Int-Ball
actuator_type: 12 internal impellers (fans)

name: Int-Ball2
desc: Second-generation Int-Ball, launched to the ISS in February 2024. Improved autonomous navigation using stereo vision (replacing ultrasonic sensors), higher-resolution 4K camera, AI-based image processing, and longer battery life. Continues the mission of automated visual documentation inside the Kibo module while reducing astronaut workload.
actuator_type: Improved impeller propulsion

name: MEV-1
desc: Mission Extension Vehicle 1. First commercial satellite servicing spacecraft in history. Successfully docked with Intelsat IS-901 on 25 February 2020 in geostationary graveyard orbit, providing 5 years of station-keeping and attitude control to extend the host satellite's operational life. Demonstrated that on-orbit life extension is commercially viable.
actuator_type: Liquid apogee engine + hall-effect electric thrusters
payload_instruments: Rendezvous Proximity Operations and Docking (RPOD) sensors
Docking probe (engages Liquid Apogee Engine nozzle)

name: MEV-2
desc: Northrop Grumman's Mission Extension Vehicle-2 (MEV-2) docked with the Intelsat 10-02 communications satellite in 2021 to take over station-keeping and attitude control, extending the client's operational life - the second operational commercial life-extension servicer after MEV-1.
actuator_type: Liquid apogee engine + hall-effect electric thrusters

name: Mission Robotic Vehicle (MRV)
desc: Northrop Grumman's Mission Robotic Vehicle (MRV) is a next-generation servicing spacecraft equipped with robotic arms (developed with DARPA) to inspect client satellites and install Mission Extension Pods, enabling a scalable in-orbit life-extension service rather than one dedicated servicer per client.
actuator_type: Robotic arm with brushless DC motors + Hall-effect electric thrusters

name: Mission Extension Pods (MEP)
desc: Northrop Grumman's Mission Extension Pods (MEPs) are small propulsion 'jetpacks' that the Mission Robotic Vehicle attaches to a client satellite to provide years of additional station-keeping - a lighter, lower-cost alternative to a full Mission Extension Vehicle per satellite.
actuator_type: Electric propulsion (orbit control only)

name: OSAM-1 (Restore-L)
desc: NASA's OSAM-1 (On-orbit Servicing, Assembly and Manufacturing-1, formerly Restore-L) was designed to robotically rendezvous with and refuel the Landsat 7 satellite and demonstrate in-space assembly/manufacturing using dexterous robotic arms. NASA cancelled the project in 2024 amid cost and technical challenges.
also_known_as: On-orbit Servicing Assembly and Manufacturing 1, Restore-L (legacy)
actuator_type: Two 7-DOF robotic arms

name: Robonaut 2 (R2)
desc: First humanoid robot in space. Developed jointly by NASA Johnson Space Center and General Motors. Launched to the ISS on STS-133 in February 2011 initially as a torso-only humanoid restricted to a stanchion. Mobility legs added in 2014 to allow movement inside the station. Returned to Earth in 2018 for repairs after a hardware malfunction; planned to return to ISS.
operating_agency: NASA Johnson Space Center / General Motors
actuator_type: Series/torque-sensing joints; tendon-driven dexterous hands; torso-mounted processors ('thinks with its stomach'); two climbing-manipulator legs (added 2014); integrated distributed mechatronics
manufacturer_history: Developed jointly by NASA Johnson Space Center (JSC) and General Motors (GM), with Oceaneering Space Systems (Space Act Agreement, 2007). Robonaut 2 (R2) - unveiled 2010, launched to the ISS on STS-133 (Space Shuttle Discovery, Feb 24, 2011) - was the first dexterous humanoid robot in space and the first US-built robot at the station. Initially a torso-only humanoid on a stanchion; two climbing 'legs' were added in 2014. A hardware fault sidelined it from ~2015; it returned to Earth in 2018 for repairs. Lineage: R1 (1997) -> R2 (2011) -> R5/Valkyrie (2013).

name: Valkyrie (R5)
desc: Full-size bipedal humanoid built by NASA's Johnson Space Center in just 15 months for the 2013 DARPA Robotics Challenge. Designed for potential deployment in space exploration scenarios including pre-deployment site preparation on Mars. Several units placed at research institutions (MIT, IHMC, Northeastern) for continued development.
actuator_type: Series-elastic actuators (rotary SEAs in arms/legs/torso; parallel linear SEAs in waist + ankles); tendon-driven hands; 'Turbodriver' motor controller (Robonaut 2 descendant, forced-air cooled)
manufacturer_history: NASA Johnson Space Center (JSC), Houston - team leader Nicolaus Radford, with the University of Texas + Texas A&M. Valkyrie (officially 'R5') was designed/built starting Oct 2012 (prototype July 2013) in a very tight timeframe for the DARPA Robotics Challenge, drawing on JSC's Robonaut heritage. In 2016 NASA awarded Valkyrie units to MIT (Russ Tedrake), UMass Lowell/Northeastern + the University of Edinburgh for the Space Robotics Challenge. Long-term goal: precursor + human-assistive missions to the Moon + Mars.

desc: Russian humanoid robot, originally developed as FEDOR (Final Experimental Demonstration Object Research) for rescue and emergency operations by the Russian Ministry of Emergency Situations. Adapted for space testing as Skybot F-850. Launched to the ISS on the uncrewed Soyuz MS-14 in August 2019. Conducted brief manipulation experiments before returning to Earth in September 2019. Mixed results — struggled in microgravity.

Conducted Japan's first 'robot conversation in space' on 7 August 2013.

name: ELSA-d
desc: Astroscale's ELSA-d (End-of-Life Services by Astroscale-demonstration, 2021) was a two-spacecraft mission - a servicer and a client - that demonstrated repeated magnetic capture and release of a client satellite in orbit, proving core technologies for future debris removal.
payload_instruments: Client satellite with magnetic plate (105 kg)

name: ADRAS-J
desc: Astroscale's ADRAS-J (Active Debris Removal by Astroscale-Japan, 2024) rendezvoused with and closely inspected a derelict Japanese H-IIA rocket upper stage - the first commercial mission to safely approach and survey a large piece of real space debris, a key step toward future removal.

name: ELSA-M
desc: Astroscale's ELSA-M is a commercial debris-removal servicer designed to capture and de-orbit multiple defunct satellites in a single mission, building on ELSA-d to provide an operational end-of-life service for satellite operators.
payload_instruments: Magnetic capture plate (compatible with OneWeb satellites)

name: ClearSpace-1
desc: ClearSpace-1 is an ESA-contracted active-debris-removal mission led by Swiss startup ClearSpace, designed to rendezvous with and capture a derelict payload adapter using a four-arm tentacle-like capture mechanism, then de-orbit it - one of the first dedicated debris-capture missions.
actuator_type: Four-armed robotic capture system (clamping mechanism)
payload_instruments: Four robotic arms with clamping jaws

name: B1 (Black Line)
desc: Lighter, faster Black Line grid robot with a cavity design roughly half the footprint of the R5. Uses individual direct-drive wheel motors and a swappable BattPack lithium-ion battery, giving about 75% higher acceleration and ~20% higher bin throughput than the R5, and can carry taller bins.
highlights: Cavity design ~half the size of R5

name: Origin
desc: The original, category-defining LocusBot — a nimble goods-to-person AMR built for collaborative, high-volume order fulfillment. Works alongside human pickers to roughly double productivity by eliminating walking time, and supports dynamic task-interleaving of picking and putaway. Configurable with multi-level shelving and a range of containers, using LiDAR and vision navigation. Sold via Robots-as-a-Service.

name: MiR250
desc: Compact, agile autonomous mobile robot from MiR (Teradyne) carrying up to 250 kg at 2 m/s. With a 580×800 mm footprint and ~30 cm height it slips through gaps as narrow as 80 cm and uses lifts and doors autonomously, navigating by laser scanners and 3D cameras under MiR Fleet. Modular tops (Hook, Top Roller, shelf lift) adapt it to many tasks.
api: MiR Fleet; REST API; WMS integration

name: MiR600
desc: IP52-rated pallet-transport AMR from MiR moving up to 600 kg at 2 m/s — the first IP52-rated AMR on the market, able to withstand dust and water drops for more demanding environments. Designed to ISO 3691-4 safety standards, with modular pallet-lifter and conveyor tops and MiR Fleet orchestration.

name: MiR1350
desc: MiR's most powerful AMR, moving loaded pallets and heavy goods up to 1,350 kg on a 1,304×864 mm load surface. IP52-rated with 13 TÜV-certified safety features and ISO 3691-4 compliance, it pairs pallet-lifter tops with MiR Fleet for autonomous heavy intralogistics.

name: OTTO 100
desc: Strong, agile light-duty AMR from OTTO Motors (Rockwell Automation) that moves boxes, bins and carts up to 150 kg at 2 m/s through person-to-person workflows. An integrated lift works with carts, laser and 3D-camera sensors enable autonomous navigation, and the rugged body is built to shrug off forklift collisions.

name: OTTO 600
desc: Tough, nimble mid-payload AMR from OTTO Motors moving up to 600 kg through high-traffic, tight spaces. The narrowest footprint in its class with an all-metal IP54 body; two forward cameras plus dual 360° corner LiDARs handle perception, and rapid-access drawers make single-person servicing simple.

name: OTTO 1500
desc: Heavy-duty workhorse AMR from OTTO Motors that moves up to 1,900 kg at top speeds of 2 m/s, even around turns, in demanding industrial environments. Built on a proven chassis introduced in 2015 with 4M+ hours of operational runtime, it supports a wide range of attachments and a modular top panel for quick servicing.
highlights: Up to 1,900 kg payload at 2 m/s

name: Proteus
desc: Amazon's first fully autonomous mobile robot, built to operate in the same open floor space as employees rather than caged areas. It autonomously lifts and moves wheeled GoCarts of packages through fulfillment and sort centers, projecting a green light ahead and stopping if a person steps into its path. Named after a moon of Neptune; used internally across Amazon's network (not sold commercially).
highlights: Works in open, shared human spaces

name: Hercules
desc: Amazon Robotics drive unit — the modern successor to the Kiva drives — that slides under inventory pods and lifts up to ~567 kg (1,250 lb) to bring goods to stationary pickers. A forward-facing 3D camera identifies people, pods and other robots for safe, fast decisions, and thousands coordinate per site as a fleet under centralized planning. First widely deployed mobile robot certified to Safety Integrity Level (SIL) 2.

name: Flow 2
navigation: TwinAI dual HD RGB cameras + VLM (10 TOPS)
desc: The Narwal Flow 2 is Narwal's 2026 flagship robot vacuum-mop, built around its signature FlowWash mopping system: a continuously self-cleaning rolling track mop (treadmill-style) that rinses in real time with up to 140°F hot water, presses down at 12 N, and uses dual water tanks with 16 nozzles plus a scraper to separate dirty water — giving far more floor contact and dwell time than spinning pads or thin rollers. On the vacuum side it delivers 31,000 Pa of suction with a DualFlow dual anti-tangle brush system (dual short rollers + long-bristle side brush) for an SGS-certified 0% tangle rate and excellent pet-hair pickup. Navigation runs on TwinAI: dual HD RGB cameras and a VLM 'brain' on a 10-TOPS processor that recognise an effectively unlimited range of objects down to 5 mm (and even locate keys or wallets), with all visuals processed locally under TÜV-certified privacy. The 95 mm slim body crosses 40 mm thresholds and lifts its mop 12 mm on carpet. A maintenance-free dock self-empties to a reusable 2.5 L bag (up to 120 days), washes mops with heated water, warm-air dries, dispenses detergent, and offers an auto refill/drain plumbing option. Freo Mind 4.0, NarGPT voice, video call and Matter included. US price $1,499.99.

desc: The ECOVACS Deebot X12 OmniCyclone is Ecovacs' 2026 flagship robot vacuum-mop (launched April 2026, CES 2026 reveal), built around two standout ideas: a bagless OmniCyclone dock and FocusJet stain pre-dissolving. The PureCyclone 2.0 dock uses dual-stage cyclonic separation (under 1% suction loss) into a reusable 1.6 L bin for up to 48 days hands-free — no consumable bags. FocusJet detects dried-on stains and pre-sprays high-pressure heated water (arch-pattern jets) before the OZMO Roller 3.0 self-washing mop — a 10.6-inch roller, 50% longer than the prior gen, spinning at 220 RPM with 15 mm carpet lift and an auto-deploying carpet shield — scrubs them away. On the vacuum side a BLAST airflow system delivers 22 L/s airflow and up to 22,000 Pa suction with ZeroTangle 4.0 anti-tangle (100% pet-hair pickup, 0% tangles on 7-inch hair). PowerBoost GaN fast-charging restores 13% in 3 minutes for 200+ min effective runtime, and AGENT YIKO 2.0 handles voice, scheduling and adaptive cleaning. Matter, live video and TruEdge 3.0 edge cleaning included. US price $1,499.

name: Omni S2
desc: The Eufy Omni S2 is Eufy's (Anker) 2026 flagship robot vacuum-mop, a CES 2026 Home Appliance honoree built around long-lasting suction and roller-mop mopping. Its AeroTurbo 2.0 system delivers up to 30,000 Pa (100 AW) with multi-cyclone separation to hold suction over time, paired with a DuoSpiral split main brush and extending side brush for anti-tangle pet-hair pickup (perfect 7-inch hair test). The HydroJet 2.0 self-cleaning roller mop scrubs at 240 RPM with 15 N pressure using electrolyzed water, lifting up to 2 inches to keep carpets dry. CleanMind AI navigation (3D MatrixEye ToF + RGB camera) recognises 200+ obstacles down to ~1 cm, crosses 42 mm thresholds, and earned a flawless 24/24 obstacle test. The 12-in-1 UniClean station auto-empties to a 2.5 L bag (~68 days), hot-washes mops at 140°F, hot-air dries, refills, dispenses detergent, and sterilises with electrolyzed water (99.9% germ reduction). A built-in fragrance diffuser freshens rooms for up to 120 hours, and it's compatible with Eufy's MarsWalker stair-climbing platform for multi-floor cleaning. Matter, Alexa and Google supported. US price $1,599.

name: Mobius 60
desc: The MOVA Mobius 60 is the 2026 flagship robot vacuum-mop from MOVA (a Dreame sub-brand), the centerpiece of MOVA's CES 2026 lineup and its first model with an automatic mop-swapping dock. Its headline MopSwap system stores three specialized pads — ThermoHold (phase-change heat-lock for greasy kitchens), Plush (soft fibres for delicate wood floors) and HyperClean (all-around) — and swaps them automatically by cleaning zone to cut cross-contamination. It delivers a class-leading 30,000 Pa suction with a Dynamic Suction Retention baffle that seals over carpet for deep pickup, a TroboWave DuoBrush triple anti-tangle system (99.99% hair removal), and spinning mop pads at 12 N / 260 RPM with 10.5 mm carpet lift. StepMaster 2.0 robotic legs clear thresholds up to 80 mm, while FlexScope navigation uses a retractable dToF LiDAR plus AI SmartSight structured-light 3D scanner (240+ objects, LED fill light) — the turret drops to 89.5 mm to slip under low furniture and rises for panoramic mapping. The all-in-one dock auto-empties to a 3.2 L bag, refills, hot-washes pads at 100°C with JetSpray drying and UV sterilisation. Raw power and obstacle avoidance are top-tier (though real-world cleaning is around average and it's loud at 78 dB max). US price $1,599 (often ~$1,299).

desc: The Dreame X60 Max Ultra Complete is Dreame's 2026 flagship robot vacuum-mop, unveiled at CES 2026 and ranked #1 overall by Vacuum Wars on launch. Its headline trick is a 3.13-inch (79.5 mm) ultra-slim body — Dreame's lowest-profile robot — that still climbs thresholds up to 88 mm via retractable robotic legs (ProLeap 2.0). It pairs 35,000 Pa of suction (through a retractable-plate sealed DuoBrush chamber) with dual AI cameras, retractable LiDAR and Proactive Illumination for 280+ object recognition down to 1 cm. Mopping uses dual spinning pads at 15 N pressure with 40°C warm water and a class-leading 21.5 mm mop lift plus an extending edge mop, scoring 89% carpet deep-clean and a rare 100% pet-hair pickup. The 10-in-1 dock self-empties (3.2 L, ~100 days), washes mops with 100°C water, hot-air dries, auto-refills and dispenses dual cleaning solutions. A 6,400 mAh battery gives ~180 min runtime (fast-charge 9-80% in 80 min) at a quiet 55 dB. Matter, Alexa/Siri/Google, pet care and rich app control round it out. US price $1,699.99.

The X60 Max Ultra Complete (CES 2026; ~$1,899) is Dreame's 2026 flagship + the industry's thinnest robot vacuum at 3.13 in (79.5 mm) - a retractable-LiDAR slim body paired with 51 mm (2 in) threshold climbing. 'Upgraded from the X50 series', it jumps to 35,000 Pa suction (from the X50's 20,000), uses the HyperStream DuoDivide anti-tangle brush + extending side brush, dual warm-water spinning mops (15 N pressure, 21.5 mm lift, extending edge mop, removable), and binocular AI cameras + Proactive Illumination (detects 1 cm objects, 280+ obstacles). Vacuum Wars measured a 100% flattened-pet-hair pickup in testing.

name: PowerDetect UV Reveal
mop_type: HyperSonic mopping (7× scrubbing vs Matrix); flat pad extends to side
navigation: NeuroNav AI (RGB sensors + lasers + UltraRange camera)
desc: The Shark PowerDetect UV Reveal (model RV3020XE) is SharkNinja's 2026 flagship robot vacuum-mop and the first robot engineered with a UV light to detect invisible stains — UV Stain Detect spots sticky spills and dried-on pet messes, then concentrates HyperSonic mopping (a vibrating pad scrubbing ~100 times per minute, 7x the scrubbing power of earlier Sharks) to remove them. Its PowerDetect suite of sensors (Dirt, Edge, Floor, Stain, Obstacle) auto-adjusts suction, scrubbing and navigation in real time, while NeverStuck technology uses chassis lift to clear higher thresholds and raise the mop to protect carpets. NeuroNav AI mapping pairs RGB sensors, lasers and an UltraRange camera for obstacle avoidance (a best-ever 20/24 for a Shark robot). The bagless NeverTouch ThermaCharged Pro dock auto-empties (~60 days), self-refills, hot-washes the mop at 185°F and dries at 175°F, removing 99.99% of bacteria from the pad. Vacuuming scored 88% carpet deep-clean with strong pet-hair pickup; the main trade-offs are heavy mopping water use and single-floor mapping. US price $1,299.99.
mop_lift: Yes (auto-lift on carpet; auto-park in base)
stain_detection: UV Reveal (UV light exposes biological residue)

name: EksoNR
desc: The clinical standard for rehabilitation walking. EksoNR’s SmartAssist software adapts help to each patient, and it was the first exoskeleton FDA-cleared for stroke and acquired brain injury, later expanded to SCI and MS.
actuator_type: Electric hip + knee actuation

name: Ekso Indego Personal
desc: Notable for being modular and light: Indego breaks into five pieces that assemble around a seated user, weighs ~12 kg, and is FDA-cleared for both clinical rehabilitation and personal use. Originally developed at Vanderbilt University.
actuator_type: Modular powered hip-knee exoskeleton (5-piece, self-assembled)

name: EksoEVO
desc: A passive industrial vest, not a powered medical device. Ekso EVO supports raised arms using spring tension — no motors or battery — transferring overhead-work load to the hips. Widely deployed in automotive and aerospace assembly.
actuator_type: Passive spring-supported upper-body vest

name: ReWalk Personal 6.0
desc: The best-known personal exoskeleton, commercially available since 2012. The 6th-generation ReWalk Personal is custom-built to each user’s measurements, drops the shoulder backpack of earlier models, and reaches 0.71 m/s — the fastest of any exoskeleton of its era. FDA-cleared and adopted by the US Department of Veterans Affairs.
actuator_type: Electric hip + knee actuation, tilt-sensor gait triggering
control_method: Tilt-sensor gait initiation from center-of-gravity shifts (crutches required)

name: ReStore
desc: A lightweight soft exosuit rather than a rigid frame. ReStore uses textile components and a cable-driven actuator to assist ankle movement during post-stroke gait therapy, making it one of the lightest clinical rehabilitation exoskeletons. FDA-cleared in 2019.
actuator_type: Soft exo-suit, powered ankle plantarflexion assist

name: HAL (Hybrid Assistive Limb)
desc: The original wearable cyborg. Cyberdyne’s HAL reads faint bioelectric (EMG) signals on the skin before the muscle moves, then drives powered hip and knee joints to assist — the medical lower-limb suit weighs ~23 kg, runs ~2h40m per charge, and was the first robot certified to the ISO 13482 personal-care safety standard. FDA-cleared in the US in 2018.
actuator_type: Electric (EMG/bioelectric intention control)

name: Cray X
desc: The first fully connected industrial exoskeleton. The 5th-generation Cray X is a carbon-fiber power suit giving up to 30 kg of lift support plus active walking assistance, running a full 8-hour shift on hot-swappable 40 V batteries. IP54-rated, it streams ergonomic telemetry to German Bionic’s AI and is used at BMW, IKEA and DPD.
actuator_type: Electric (smart/connected)
use_cases: Industrial lifting injury prevention (BMW, IKEA, DPD)
assist_force: Up to 30 kg (66 lb) per lift
control_method: Dual servo motors, AI-adaptive (Smart Safety Companion)

name: Apogee
desc: German Bionic’s 6th-generation suit, leaner and lighter than the Cray X, with dual-motor support for lifting (up to 30 kg) and walking. The Apogee Ultra shown at CES 2025 pushes assist to 80 lb (36 kg), targeting baggage handling, construction and nursing.
actuator_type: Electric (smart/connected)

name: Atalante X
desc: The first crutchless self-balancing walking exoskeleton. Atalante X balances itself across 12 powered joints, freeing the patient’s hands entirely during gait therapy. CE-marked, deployed in rehab clinics across Europe and the US.
actuator_type: 12 powered joints (hips, knees, ankles), self-balancing dynamic walking

name: Eve
desc: Eve is Wandercraft's personal exoskeleton — billed as the world's first self-balancing exoskeleton for personal use that works hands-free, without crutches or a walker. Built by the Paris-based robotics firm (founded 2012, 30+ patents) on the same proven platform as its FDA-cleared Atalante X rehabilitation system, Eve has a fully powered lower body with 12 actuated degrees of freedom across the hips, knees and ankles, using AI-driven dynamic balance to let people with severe mobility impairments — such as spinal cord injuries or MS — stand and walk in everyday settings. Users typically need about five training sessions. Unveiled as a prototype in 2023, Eve entered clinical trials in 2025 (including at the James J. Peters VA Medical Center and the Kessler Institute) and was carried in the 2024 Paris Olympic torch relay; commercial availability is targeted for around 2026, backed by a strategic partnership with Renault Group.
actuator_type: Electric (powered hip-knee-ankle)
manufacturer_history: Wandercraft (Paris, France). Medical exoskeleton pioneer (Atalante self-balancing exo); developing Calvin industrial humanoid built on its self-balancing gait tech.

name: X-ble Shoulder
desc: Hyundai's X-ble Shoulder is a passive industrial wearable that supports overhead work, reducing shoulder-muscle load; part of Hyundai Robotics' wearable robot line (alongside earlier VEX/CEX) aimed at factory ergonomics.
actuator_type: Passive/spring module

name: MATE-XT
desc: A passive, batteryless shoulder exoskeleton from Comau weighing ~3 kg. MATE-XT mirrors arm movements with spring support across 8 levels and resists dust, UV and water for outdoor use in agriculture, construction and shipbuilding.
actuator_type: Passive spring (no motor)

name: Paexo Shoulder
desc: One of the lightest industrial exoskeletons at just 1.9 kg. Ottobock’s Paexo Shoulder is passive, transferring the weight of raised arms from the shoulders to the hips during overhead assembly. Deployed at Volkswagen.
actuator_type: Passive mechanical
control_method: Mechanical weight transfer to hips (no battery)

name: MyoPro
desc: A powered arm brace controlled by the wearer’s own body. MyoPro reads EMG signals from a weakened arm and drives a powered elbow and hand to complete the intended motion.
actuator_type: Myoelectric (surface EMG)
control_method: EMG signals from the wearer’s own arm

name: Ascend
desc: A featherweight exoskeleton that runs on air. Roam’s Ascend uses lightweight pneumatic actuation instead of motors, sensing movement to assist the knee — aimed at osteoarthritis and general mobility.
actuator_type: Pneumatic textile

name: Carbonhand
desc: A soft robotic glove that adds strength to a human grip. Carbonhand’s fingertip sensors detect grasping, then artificial tendons add up to ~20% more force — used medically for weak hands and industrially to prevent strain.
actuator_type: SEM (Soft Extra Muscle) tendon
control_method: Fingertip pressure sensors + artificial tendons (SEM technology)

name: REX
desc: A self-supporting exoskeleton that stands on its own — no crutches required. REX bears its full weight independently and is joystick-driven, letting users with significant paralysis stand, walk and exercise hands-free.
actuator_type: Self-supporting powered legs, joystick control (no crutches)

name: Stretch 3
desc: Hello Robot's Stretch 3 is a lightweight (~24.5 kg) mobile manipulator built for research and assistive robotics - a wheeled base with a telescoping lift arm and dexterous wrist/gripper, fully ROS 2 native. Designed for in-home and lab manipulation studies at a fraction of the cost of traditional research arms.

name: Husky UGV
desc: The Clearpath Husky is a rugged medium-sized unmanned ground vehicle widely used in robotics research (including Mars robotics work at NASA/MIT). Large payload and power capacity, all-terrain differential drive, fully ROS 2 supported - the go-to outdoor research UGV.

name: Jackal UGV
desc: The Clearpath Jackal is a compact, weatherproof unmanned ground vehicle with onboard computer, GPS and IMU, used for outdoor autonomy, mapping and demining research. Comprehensive ROS API; popular in academia.

name: Dingo
desc: The Clearpath Dingo is a lightweight indoor mobile robot for research and education, available in differential or omnidirectional drive, used for navigation, mobile manipulation and mapping studies.

name: Ridgeback
desc: The Clearpath Ridgeback is an indoor omnidirectional mobile base designed to carry manipulators and heavy payloads, using mecanum-style wheels for precise forward, lateral and twisting motion - a common base for mobile-manipulation research.
actuator_type: Omnidirectional mecanum drive

name: Warthog UGV
desc: The Clearpath Warthog is a large amphibious all-terrain UGV for rugged outdoor research - capable on land, mud, snow and water - with high payload and ROS support for field robotics.
actuator_type: Amphibious skid-steer (land + water)

name: TurtleBot 4
desc: TurtleBot 4 is the world's leading low-cost open-source ROS 2 mobile robot, built on iRobot's Create 3 base with a Raspberry Pi 4, 2D LiDAR and OAK-D camera. The de-facto entry platform for learning ROS 2; available in Lite and Standard.

name: TurtleBot 3
desc: TurtleBot 3 (ROBOTIS, 2017) is a small, affordable, highly modular ROS mobile robot for education and research, available in Burger and Waffle Pi variants, with 360° LiDAR and Dynamixel actuators - a SLAM/navigation learning staple.

name: Human Support Robot (HSR)
desc: Toyota's Human Support Robot (HSR) is a compact, cylindrical mobile manipulator with a folding arm and omnidirectional base, developed for assistive and human-support research. It anchors the RoboCup@Home Domestic Standard Platform League.
cameras: RGB-D head camera + stereo + wide-angle cameras

name: Fetch
desc: The Fetch mobile manipulator (Fetch Robotics, now Zebra) pairs a round mobile base with a 7-DOF arm and adjustable-height torso, widely used in manipulation and warehouse-automation research; typically paired with the Freight base-only platform.

name: PR2
desc: The Willow Garage PR2 (Personal Robot 2) was the seminal dual-arm mobile-manipulation research platform that catalysed the ROS ecosystem. Two 7-DOF arms, an omnidirectional base and rich sensing - hugely influential, now discontinued but historically pivotal.

name: iCub
desc: An open-source, child-size humanoid testbed for embodied-cognition and AI research, designed by the EU-funded RobotCub Consortium (2004–2009) and built by the Italian Institute of Technology in Genoa. About 104 cm and 22 kg, iCub has 53 actuated degrees of freedom — 7 per arm, 9 per hand (across 19 underactuated joints), 6 per leg, plus torso, neck and eyes — and a rich sensor suite: stereo camera eyes, microphones, IMU, joint force/torque sensors and a capacitive tactile skin of ~2,000 sensing points. It runs Debian Linux with the YARP middleware and is fully open-source under GPL. Roughly 30 iCubs are in labs worldwide; a jet-powered flying variant (iRonCub) has even been explored.
actuator_type: Brushless electric motors + Harmonic Drive 1/100; torso + shoulder tendon-driven/coupled; legs with Series Elastic Actuators (removable springs, from CoMAN)

Sized like a 3.5-4-year-old child, it's a benchmark for embodied cognition. Variants incl. HeiCub (no head/arms) and the adult-size iCub 3 teleoperation avatar (2021).

name: ALOHA 2 (Stationary)
desc: Trossen's ALOHA platform (based on the Stanford ALOHA project) is a low-cost bimanual teleoperation-and-imitation-learning system using paired leader/follower WidowX arms - a key platform for robot-learning and dexterous-manipulation research.
actuator_type: 2x leader + 2x follower arms (bimanual teleoperation)

name: Reachy 2
desc: A fully open-source bimanual humanoid from France's Pollen Robotics (acquired by Hugging Face in April 2025), launched October 2024 as a body for embodied-AI research. Reachy 2 stands 136–166 cm, weighs 50 kg, and pairs two 7-DoF bio-inspired arms — built on Pollen's Orbita 2D/3D compliant joints — each lifting ~3 kg through a parallel torque-controlled gripper. An expressive head (asymmetric eyes and antennas) plus stereo RGB, an Orbbec RGB-D and a ToF sensor give rich perception, and a three-omniwheel mobile base with RPLIDAR S2 handles navigation. VR teleoperation runs at ~125 ms glass-to-glass latency; the platform is ROS2-based with a Python SDK, LeRobot and MuJoCo/Gazebo support, and ships in single/dual-arm and stationary/mobile configurations. 100+ deployed across 20 countries.
cameras: 2x IMX296 global-shutter RGB (stereo) + Orbbec Gemini 336 RGB-D + Luxonis OAK ToF

Made Poppy (early 3D-printed open humanoid) → Reachy (CES 2020) → Reachy 2 (CES 2025). Acquired by Hugging Face April 2025 (open-sourcing HW+SW). Reachy Mini ($299 desktop).
